audit_scope.motivation: A screw/nut or two-helix interlock can fix a relative registry and oppose relative rotation. The audit tests whether that new relational datum can source an absolute Z12 origin and an orientation polarity without importing an anchor.
audit_scope.finite_abstraction: Two helix phases a,b in Z12, pitch labels p_A,p_B in U(12), a relative registry delta=b-a, and a lock predicate L(p_A,p_B,delta).
audit_scope.nonclaim: This is not a claim that a DNA double helix is literally a cosmic screw/nut mechanism, nor that a mechanical analogy is a strict nadsoliton source law.

inputs.P3131: Epsilon_OT requires a support-local section law coupling a nontranslation twist to a support representative.
inputs.P3129: Gamma_SO requires both a nonzero sign and a source-origin representative.
inputs.P2718: The chiral bispectrum gives a nonzero orientation marker but lacks a non-premise origin and torsor coupling.

formal_model.interlock_predicate: L(p_A,p_B,delta) = true means that the two helices have a permitted, locked relative registry.
formal_model.lock_effect: A fixed relative registry removes independent relative rotation, but preserves the full diagonal global-phase action because delta(a+t,b+t)=delta(a,b).
formal_model.inversion: I(a,b,epsilon_A,epsilon_B) = (-a,-b,-epsilon_A,-epsilon_B); it maps a chiral lock to its opposite-polarity partner unless a signed source law selects one.
formal_model.candidate_section: Zeta_OS^HL([H]) = an absolute support representative x in Z12 derived from the locked pair, not from a chart label or external anchor.

proof: Fix p_A, p_B and a permitted delta_0. The lock locus is {(a,a+delta_0): a in Z12}; it has 12 elements.
The diagonal action t maps (a,a+delta_0) to (a+t,a+t+delta_0), stays in the same lock locus, and is free for generic locked pairs.
Therefore the lock removes relative rotation but leaves exactly one twelve-element common-rotation/global-phase orbit.

If a quotient-level source-free section s chose an absolute origin, quotient invariance gives s([a,b])=s([a+t,b+t]), while origin covariance would require s([a+t,b+t])=s([a,b])+t. For t=1 these statements contradict each other in Z12.
A raw-coordinate rule such as x=a is equivariant but is not a source: it merely imports the phase label already present in H.
An inversion-odd chirality label can distinguish the two relative-handedness branches only conditionally; without an exported signed source law its polarity remains paired.

acceptance_gates: strict nadsoliton provenance rather than a mechanical analogy
relative registry fixed without chart-label convention
absolute origin sourced after quotienting the diagonal Z12 action
unique polarity coupling to the P2708/P2714 orientation torsor
no selector, apparatus, observed-light, Planck-unit, Lagrangian-normalization, bridge, role-transfer, L_total, or ToE import

decision.bounded_result: The interlocked-helical relation is a genuinely new typed candidate and captures the useful part of the screw/nut intuition: it can constrain relative phase and eliminate independent relative rotation. It does not, by itself, fix common global rotation, an absolute Z12 origin, or a chiral polarity. Consequently Zeta_OS^HL is a relative-lock witness, not an import-free support-local section or Gamma_SO source.
decision.next_honest_step: Do not turn a relative lock into a fictitious absolute anchor. Reopen this route only if one explicit strict formula/artifact exports a nontranslation, support-local helical-lock defect D_HL with both a nonzero inversion-odd value and a coupling to one support representative. Its provenance, stabilizer behavior, and torsor polarity must be audited before any Zeta_OS/Gamma_SO retest. Otherwise preserve the P3131-P3132 no-absolute-section boundary.

replay_boundaries: Do not use a chosen screw axis, a labelled DNA base, a boundary clamp, a lexicographic phase, or an apparatus mark as an internal source.
Do not identify a physical DNA molecule or an ordinary screw/nut with the nadsoliton without an explicit source theorem.
Do not promote relative locking to QW-2191 discharge, selector closure, unit/action normalization, L_total, bridge completion, role transfer, or ToE closure.
